title: Recreating mouse cortico-hippocampal neuronal circuit in microfluidic devices to study BDNF axonal transport upon glucocorticoid treatment
protocol: Weigh 50 g of silicon elastomer (PDMS) and 5 g of curing agent.
Stir the mixture vigorously for 2–3 minutes.
Transfer the PDMS and curing agent mixture into two 50 mL conical tubes.
Centrifuge the mixture for 2 minutes at 210 × g at a temperature between 15°C and 25°C.
Fill epoxy resins with the PDMS mixture.
Incubate the filled resins under vacuum for 1 hour at a temperature between 15°C and 25°C to remove air bubbles.
Allow the PDMS to polymerize for 3 hours at 60°C in an oven.
Unmold the polymerized PDMS pattern from the epoxy resin using a micropipette tip.
Punch microfluidic chambers out of the unmolded PDMS.
Fill four molds with PDMS.
Unmold solid PDMS patterns using a pipette tip after polymerization in the oven.
Punch the unmolded PDMS patterns to generate wells.
Cut around the pattern with a scalpel blade.
Punch three synaptic wells with a 2.5 mm punch.
Punch other wells with a 3 mm punch.
Wash PDMS microchambers with 96% ethanol.
Place microchambers in a 50 mL conical tube filled with 25 mL of 96% ethanol.
Sonicate the microchambers (3 × 15 s) using an ultrasound cleaning bath.
Shake the conical tube gently between rounds of sonication.
Wash microchambers three times with autoclaved Milli-Q water.
Dry the microchambers with a compressed air blow gun.
Incubate the microchambers at 60°C for 30 minutes in the oven.
Place the PDMS microchambers and glass-bottom Petri dishes into a plasma cleaner under vacuum for 30 seconds.
Stick the PDMS microchambers to the glass at the bottom of the Petri dish with the pattern side facing down.
Incubate the Petri dishes in an oven at 60°C for 15 minutes.
Place the lids of the Petri dishes face down and the micro chambers stuck to the Petri dishes in a plasma cleaner for 10 seconds under vacuum.
Close the Petri dishes with their lids after plasma cleaning.
Sterilize the microchambers contained in the Petri dishes for 20 minutes under the UV lamp of a culture hood while keeping the Petri dish lids closed.
Sterilize a 12 cm Petri dish containing a piece of Whatman filter paper under the hood.
Humidify the Whatman filter paper with sterile water and place small Petri dishes in the 12 cm Petri dish for a humidified environment.
Coat the upper and synaptic chambers with 20 μL of poly-D-lysine (0.1 mg/mL).
Fill the postsynaptic chamber with 20 μL of a mix of poly-D-lysine (0.1 mg/mL) and laminin (10 μg/mL).
Incubate the microchambers for 12 h at 4°C.
Remove any bubbles that may form when pipetting the coating medium into the microchambers.
Rinse the coated microfluidic devices three times with filtered Neurobasal medium under a culture hood.
Fill the microchambers with growth medium and place them at 37°C in a tissue-culture incubator.
Prepare 50 mL of growth medium under the cell culture hood.
Filter sterilize the prepared solutions.
Fill a 35 mm Petri dish with DM Ky/Mg.
Place the Petri dish on ice with the lid closed.
Fill two 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes with 1 mL of DM Ky/Mg each and label them “cortex” and “hippocampus.”
Place the labeled Eppendorf tubes on ice.
Prepare 100 mL of 1× PBS from 10× PBS and fill a 12 cm Petri dish.
Close the lid and place the Petri dish on ice.
Wipe the dissection bench clean with 70% ethanol.
Immerse cleaned forceps and surgical scissors into 70% ethanol.
Wipe clean the stereological microscope platform with 70% ethanol.
Anesthetize the mouse by intraperitoneal injection of 100 mg/kg ketamine and 10 mg/kg xylazine.
Check the absence of reflexes by pitching the tip of the tail.
Place the animal in dorsal decubitus position.
Disinfect the lower abdomen part of the mouse with 70% ethanol.
Make a 1–2 cm mid ventral incision in the skin with surgical scissors, the round tip facing the muscular plane.
Incise the abdominal muscle fibers, the round tip facing the abdominal cavity.
Extract the uterine horns by cutting and cut the extremities.
Rinse the uterine horns in 1× PBS contained in a Petri dish.
Incise the uterine horns with fine straight-tip scissors to clear embryos from their amniotic sac and placenta.
Transfer rinsed embryos into the Petri dish containing DM Ky/Mg previously chilled at 4°C.
Decapitate the fetuses under a stereological microscope.
Remove the skin and skull with tweezers.
Dissect out the meninges using fine straight-tip forceps.
Dissect out the cortex and hippocampus using fine straight-tip forceps.
Transfer the cortices into Eppendorf tubes maintained on ice.
Transfer the hippocampi into Eppendorf tubes maintained on ice.
Transfer the brain structures into a 15 mL conical tube under the tissue-culture hood.
Wait for the structures to sediment and discard the supernatant.
Add 2 mL of optiMEM glucose and repeat the previous step two times.
Mechanically dissociate the structures in optiMEM glucose by repeated pipetting with a Pasteur pipette.
Count the cells using a Malassez hemocytometer.
Pipette the volume corresponding to 5 × 10^6 neurons.
Centrifuge the cells at 60 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the neurons in 100 μL of growth medium.
Plate the neurons on the microfluidics device.
Remove the growth medium contained in the microchambers.
Add 6 μL of growth medium to each well in the synaptic chamber.
Add 2 μL of cortical neuron suspension to the presynaptic compartment.
Add 2 μL of hippocampal cell suspension to the postsynaptic compartment.
Incubate the devices for 1 hour in the incubator.
Fill all compartments with up to 20 μL of growth medium after 1 hour.
Warm up growth medium to 37°C before addition to the cells.
Infect neurons with lentivirus (LV) on DIV1.
Dilute 0.2 μL virus in 15 μL growth medium per microchamber.
Remove the medium of the presynaptic compartment.
Add 15 μL of LV.CMV.BDNF-mCherry to the presynaptic compartment.
Incubate for 24 h.
After 24 h (DIV2), remove the virus.
Fill the microchambers with growth medium (20 μL).
Regularly check and add 10 μL fresh medium once per week to maintain 20 μL volume of growth medium.
Humidify the Whatman paper with autoclaved distilled water once per week.
Treat cells for 3 h with 5 μM of DXM on DIV12.
Image using a spinning disk confocal system.
Prepare DXM at 50 μM by diluting 1 μL of 10 mM DXM in 200 μL growth medium.
Warm the solution up to ensure complete dissolution and agitation.
Add 2 μL of 50 μM DXM to the left wells feeding the pre- and postsynaptic compartments.
Incubate treated cells for 3 h in a CO2 incubator.
Record live cells using an inverted microscope coupled with a spinning disk confocal system connected to a wide field electron-multiplying CCD camera.
Maintain cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 during recording.
Acquire images every 200 ms for 30 s to study BDNF-mCherry trafficking using a 63× oil-immersion objective with a numerical aperture of 1.46.
Perform five acquisitions per microchamber and three microchambers per condition.
After treatment, fix neurons in 4% paraformaldehyde if immunostaining is required for further analysis.
